flags.description:
Read-only analytical escape hatch for cash spending and income questions that do not map cleanly to the dedicated tools. Use `search_cash_transactions` first when it fits.

SQL dialect: SQLite. One read-only `SELECT` over the table below (`WITH`, subqueries, self-joins, window, date and JSON functions all work). Results stop at 250 rows; `truncated=true` means there were more, so total in SQL.

Published logical schema:
cash_transactions(
  posted_date TEXT NOT NULL, -- 'YYYY-MM-DD'; compare to date('now', '-30 days')
  posted_month TEXT NOT NULL, -- 'YYYY-MM'
  arrived_at TEXT NULL, -- UTC time it reached Driggsby
  description TEXT NOT NULL, -- the bank's text
  merchant_name TEXT NOT NULL, -- 'Unknown Counterparty' when unnamed, never NULL
  amount REAL NOT NULL, -- never negative; direction says which way
  currency_code TEXT NULL,
  direction TEXT NOT NULL, -- 'outflow' or 'inflow'
  status TEXT NOT NULL, -- 'posted' or 'pending'
  category_primary TEXT NULL, -- a code, e.g. 'FOOD_AND_DRINK'; match exactly
  category_detailed TEXT NULL, -- e.g. 'FOOD_AND_DRINK_GROCERIES'
  transaction_semantic_type TEXT NOT NULL, -- spend, transfer, debt_payment, income, fee, interest, inflow, unknown
  counts_as_spend BOOLEAN (1 or 0) NOT NULL, -- 1 = purchases and fees; transfers (to people too) and card payments are 0 even when real expenses
  subtracts_from_spending BOOLEAN (1 or 0) NOT NULL, -- 1 for refunds
  classification_source TEXT NOT NULL, -- user_rule, user_correction or automatic
  tags JSON TEXT NOT NULL, -- JSON array of the user's tag slugs
  account_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  account_mask_last4 TEXT NULL, -- tells same-named accounts apart
  institution_name TEXT NULL,
  account_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  account_subtype TEXT NULL,
  location_city TEXT NULL, -- NULL when the bank reported none
  location_region TEXT NULL,
  payment_group TEXT NULL, -- set when a rule combined rows into one payment
  payment_group_size INTEGER NULL,
  payment_group_total REAL NULL
)

Category and cashflow guidance:
- `arrived_at` is when the row reached Driggsby, as UTC text like `2026-04-24T14:00:12Z`: a posted charge keeps its pending version's time unless its amount changed, a changed amount arrives again, and history is NULL: what came with connecting an account, rows dated before it, and rows that arrived more than 14 days after their own date. For what arrived in a window, whatever the rows' dates, filter `arrived_at >= '2026-04-24T14:00:12Z' AND arrived_at < '2026-04-25T14:00:09Z'`.
- `merchant_name` is Driggsby's best public counterparty label. Enriched rows use Driggsby's display name; other rows fall back to Plaid merchant data and transaction text. It is never NULL: rows Driggsby cannot name use the literal text `Unknown Counterparty`, so filter with `merchant_name = 'Unknown Counterparty'` — `merchant_name IS NULL` matches nothing.
- `category_primary` and `category_detailed` are Driggsby's best available category values. Enriched rows use Driggsby's PFC-derived taxonomy plus Driggsby extensions; other rows fall back to Plaid.
- Use `transaction_semantic_type`, `counts_as_spend`, and `subtracts_from_spending` for totals, cashflow, and `get_overview` reconciliation.
- `transaction_semantic_type` is Driggsby's coarse cashflow bucket with these values: `spend`, `transfer`, `debt_payment`, `income`, `fee`, `interest`, `inflow`, `unknown`.
- `counts_as_spend = true` means the row counts in Driggsby's spending totals, including ordinary purchases and bank-fee cash outflows. Transfers, debt payments, income, interest, generic inflows, and unknown rows return `false`.
- `subtracts_from_spending = true` marks refunds that subtract from Driggsby's net spending totals. It is always false when `counts_as_spend` is true. Rewards and other credits are false on both flags and never affect spending totals.
- Driggsby spending totals are NET of refunds: net spending = sum of `counts_as_spend` rows minus sum of `subtracts_from_spending` rows over the same window. A refund reduces the period it posted in, even when the original purchase was in an earlier period, so a period's net spending can be negative.
- Use exact category string matches for category breakdowns, for example `category_primary = 'FOOD_AND_DRINK'`, `category_detailed = 'FOOD_AND_DRINK_GROCERIES'`, or `category_detailed = 'INCOME_SALARY'`.
- `classification_source` says where the row's category came from: `user_rule` (one of the user's transaction rules), `user_correction` (a category the user pinned), or `automatic` (Driggsby's classification). A user-set category also decides `transaction_semantic_type` and `counts_as_spend`.
- `tags` is a JSON array of the slugs the user's rules put on the row, `[]` when none. Tags are labels only and never change totals. Filter with `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM json_each(tags) WHERE value = 'naples-work-trip')`; `list_transaction_tags` names the workspace's tags. Which rule put a tag on a row is `tag_sources` on search_cash_transactions rows; SQL does not carry it.
- `account_name` can repeat: two accounts can share a name, bank, and type. `account_mask_last4` is the same last four digits `list_accounts` returns for each account; group by it with `account_name` to keep such accounts apart.
- `location_city` and `location_region` are the location the bank reported for the row (mostly card purchases), NULL when it reported none. Use them for place-based questions such as everything spent in one city during a trip.
- `payment_group`, `payment_group_size`, and `payment_group_total` are set on rows one of the user's transaction rules combined into a single payment (a rent sent as two transfers): every row of the payment shares the `payment_group` handle (the same value as `payment_group_ref` on search rows) and carries the payment's row count and its total (absolute, like `amount`; one currency); NULL on every other row, and NULL again once fewer than two of the payment's rows are still linked and visible (a WHERE clause that keeps one row of a payment does not change its size or total). Group by `payment_group` to count payments rather than transfers.
- To inspect rows behind current get_overview 30-day outflow buckets, use the last 30 calendar days ending today plus `status = 'posted'`, `direction = 'outflow'`, and the bucket predicate, for example `transaction_semantic_type = 'transfer'` or `transaction_semantic_type = 'debt_payment'`.
- To reconstruct current get_overview 30-day net spending, use the last 30 calendar days ending today plus `status = 'posted'` and the single-query net-spending example below: spend rows add and refund rows subtract inside one SUM.

Response notes: numbers are JSON numbers; a true/false column selected as it is comes back as a boolean, and an expression on one as 1 or 0; `tags` selected as it is comes back as a list; dates stay YYYY-MM-DD text; and `truncated=true` means Driggsby returned the first 250 rows or cut rows to stay within the response-size cap.

Examples:

Groceries last month:

```sql
SELECT posted_date, description, amount
FROM cash_transactions
WHERE direction = 'outflow' AND posted_month = '2026-03' AND category_detailed = 'FOOD_AND_DRINK_GROCERIES' AND counts_as_spend = true
ORDER BY posted_date DESC
```

Net spending for a month, in one query (spend rows add, refund rows subtract):

```sql
SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN counts_as_spend = true THEN amount ELSE -amount END) AS net_spending
FROM cash_transactions
WHERE posted_month = '2026-03' AND status = 'posted' AND (counts_as_spend = true OR subtracts_from_spending = true)
```

Spending over the last 30 days by category:

```sql
SELECT category_primary, ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS total_spend, COUNT(*) AS charges
FROM cash_transactions
WHERE counts_as_spend = true AND status = 'posted' AND posted_date >= date('now', '-30 days')
GROUP BY category_primary
ORDER BY total_spend DESC
```

Month over month spending:

```sql
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT posted_month, SUM(amount) AS spend
  FROM cash_transactions
  WHERE counts_as_spend = true
  GROUP BY posted_month
)
SELECT posted_month, spend, spend - LAG(spend) OVER (ORDER BY posted_month) AS change
FROM monthly
ORDER BY posted_month DESC
```

Top merchant per month:

```sql
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT posted_month, merchant_name, SUM(amount) AS total_outflow,
         row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY posted_month ORDER BY SUM(amount) DESC, merchant_name) AS merchant_rank
  FROM cash_transactions
  WHERE direction = 'outflow' AND counts_as_spend = true
  GROUP BY posted_month, merchant_name
)
SELECT posted_month, merchant_name, total_outflow
FROM ranked
WHERE merchant_rank = 1
ORDER BY posted_month DESC
```

Everything tagged as one trip (tag slugs come from list_transaction_tags):

```sql
SELECT posted_date, merchant_name, amount, location_city
FROM cash_transactions
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM json_each(tags) WHERE value = 'naples-work-trip') AND direction = 'outflow'
ORDER BY posted_date DESC
```

Payments a rule combined from several transfers, one row per payment:

```sql
SELECT payment_group, MIN(posted_date) AS paid_on, COUNT(*) AS transfers, SUM(amount) AS paid
FROM cash_transactions
WHERE payment_group IS NOT NULL AND category_detailed = 'RENT_AND_UTILITIES_RENT'
GROUP BY payment_group
ORDER BY paid_on DESC
```

Itemized charges: this table has every charge whole, under the charge's own category. Driggsby's Spending page counts a charge the user's agent itemized (save_transaction_items) by its items' categories instead, so for what such a charge bought, or for a category only items carry (Household, Baby), use query_item_sql.

  arrived_at TEXT NULL, -- UTC time it reached Driggsby
  name TEXT NOT NULL, -- institution's description
  ticker_symbol TEXT NULL,
  activity_type TEXT NOT NULL, -- buy, sell, dividend, interest, fee, contribution, withdrawal, transfer, cancel, other
  cash_amount REAL NOT NULL, -- never negative; cash_flow_direction says which way

```sql

FROM investment_activity
WHERE activity_type = 'dividend'
GROUP BY trade_month
ORDER BY trade_month DESC
```

Latest buy per ticker:

```sql
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT trade_date, ticker_symbol, name, cash_amount,
         row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY ticker_symbol ORDER BY trade_date DESC, name) AS trade_rank
  FROM investment_activity
  WHERE activity_type = 'buy'
)

FROM ranked
WHERE trade_rank = 1
ORDER BY trade_date DESC
```

Read-only analytical SQL over the items behind the user's itemized charges: one row per item an agent saved with `save_transaction_items`, with its charge's facts (only itemized charges have rows).

SQL dialect: SQLite. One read-only `SELECT` over the table below (`WITH`, subqueries, self-joins, window, date and JSON functions all work). Results stop at 250 rows; `truncated=true` means there were more, so total in SQL.

Published logical schema:
cash_transaction_items(
  posted_date TEXT NOT NULL, -- the charge's 'YYYY-MM-DD'; compare to date('now', '-30 days')
  posted_month TEXT NOT NULL, -- 'YYYY-MM'
  merchant_name TEXT NOT NULL, -- the charge's, as on cash_transactions
  account_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  account_mask_last4 TEXT NULL,
  direction TEXT NOT NULL, -- 'outflow' (a purchase) or 'inflow' (a refund)
  charge_amount REAL NOT NULL, -- the whole charge, never negative
  currency_code TEXT NOT NULL,
  store_name TEXT NOT NULL, -- the store the items came from
  source TEXT NOT NULL, -- 'order' or 'receipt'
  ordered_on TEXT NULL, -- 'YYYY-MM-DD' the order was placed or the receipt dated; NULL when not given
  item_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  category TEXT NOT NULL, -- an item category key, e.g. 'groceries'
  category_label TEXT NOT NULL, -- the name the user sees, e.g. 'Home Improvement'
  quantity REAL NULL,
  unit_price REAL NULL,
  amount REAL NOT NULL, -- the item's own line price
  allocated_amount REAL NOT NULL, -- its share of the charge with tax and shipping; a charge's add up to charge_amount unless stale
  items_stale BOOLEAN (1 or 0) NOT NULL, -- 1 when the charge changed after it was itemized
  counts_as_spend BOOLEAN (1 or 0) NOT NULL, -- 1 when Spending counts the charge
  subtracts_from_spending BOOLEAN (1 or 0) NOT NULL -- 1 for a refund that nets Spending
)

Response notes: numbers are JSON numbers; a true/false column selected as it is comes back as a boolean, and an expression on one as 1 or 0; dates stay YYYY-MM-DD text.

Examples:

Coffee spending by month:

```sql
SELECT posted_month, SUM(CASE WHEN direction = 'outflow' THEN allocated_amount ELSE -allocated_amount END) AS spent
FROM cash_transaction_items
WHERE (counts_as_spend = true OR subtracts_from_spending = true) AND item_name LIKE '%coffee%'
GROUP BY posted_month
ORDER BY posted_month DESC
```

Spending by item category in the last 90 days:

```sql
SELECT category_label, SUM(CASE WHEN direction = 'outflow' THEN allocated_amount ELSE -allocated_amount END) AS spent, COUNT(*) AS items
FROM cash_transaction_items
WHERE (counts_as_spend = true OR subtracts_from_spending = true) AND posted_date >= date('now', '-90 days')
GROUP BY category_label
ORDER BY spent DESC
```

flags.description: Driggsby automations run on Driggsby's servers against the user's linked accounts, on a schedule, without the user or this conversation being open. Use them instead of scheduling a task in your own tool whenever the job is about the user's money: each run is its own AI agent that reads the user's financial data with the same read tools you have here (minus CSV export), it always records its result in the user's Driggsby dashboard, and when it finds something or owes a report it messages the user in their Driggsby Activity, and by email when the automation has email on. In this version automations check and notify — they never move money. So "move $500 to Robinhood after payday" becomes an automation that checks for the deposit and tells the user "payday landed — ready to move $500 when you approve"; say exactly that to the user rather than promising the transfer. Create a new automation (omit `automation_ref`) or update an existing one (pass the `automation_ref` from list_automations; only the fields you send change). Creating needs `name`, `prompt`, `schedule_kind`, and `schedule_hour` (`weekly` also needs `schedule_weekday`; default timezone is UTC, so pass the user's IANA zone when you know it). The user's dashboard always shows every run; `notify` lists the EXTRA channels on top of that — `["email"]` (the default on create) or `[]` for dashboard-only. A name that already exists is never overwritten: the error names the existing automation and its ref so you can update it instead or pick another name. The response echoes the complete saved automation (full prompt included), so you never need to re-read it, plus a `notes` line to relay to the user about when the first check happens. To check right away, call run_automation_now with the returned automation_ref.
